I have been married for 13 years. Over those 13 years, I have occasionally brought up the topic of getting a pistol to my wife. Since we had a kid shortly after marriage, she has been against me having a gun in the house. Last year, I finally convinced her that having one was a good idea and for Christmas, I bought myself a hand gun. Little did I know I would suddenly be surrounded by generous new community.

Firstly, I just moved half way across the country last January. I know a core group of 7 folks that I work directly with and haven't had the opportunity to meet a lot of other people. When I started talking to one of them about buying a gun in October, the rest of the group chimed in and started asking a lot of questions about why I wanted a gun, what it would be used for and my experience level. They all had recommendations and advice. There were days that we spent 3 to 4 hours talking around guns. I suddenly found out that I was surrounded by a goup of diehard gun enthusiasts and had no clue the previous 10 months. All but one had no less that 7 guns and one has upwards of 30. All of a sudden, they were inviting me out to there farms to try their weapons or taking me to the gun range with a trunk full of guns in tow for me to shoot. Then the guy in charge of security heard us talking. He was an ex sheriff deputy. He brought me some quiet rounds for my wife to shoot. My wife's new friend from the neighborhood mentioned to her husband that I was getting my CCL and he called me over to look at his collection of 16 hand guns, 12 long guns and close to 10k rounds of ammunition. He told me to not by rounds and come get all I wanted. He had an old neighbor that had passed and he bought his ~10k rounds from his wife. One of my cowarkers gave me a bag of 4 handguns probably worth $2500 to bring home to my wife so she could hold and feel different types of guns.

Now almost every weekend, I am at the gun range or someone's back yard shooting my new M&p 9mm, or out of their collections, 1 of 3 custom built AR-15s, an all steel Kimber .45, a top of the line Sig .40, A matching set of Walther 9mm 1911s, a colt 45 1911 or any other choice of 80 weapons that my new best friends have lying around that they are always offering up for me to shoot.

I never knew that asking a coworker a simple question about a Glock trigger would lead to having new life long friends and a new hobby. I also never knew the gun community was so open, friendly and willing to share their knowledge, time and trust to help initiate a Newby into their world. I have been assimilated and never happier!!!! Thanks guys!!!!

I suppose I should start. I would prefer not say exactly what subculture I'm from to avoid identification. But we have all the subtlety and tact of an anvil. If a fat person walks up to us in conversation, we will not at all hesitate to say "you're fat". If we notice someone has gotten significantly larger since we last saw them, we will, almost without fail, ask "You've gained weight. Why?". It would actually be considered rude to NOT ask why they got so big.

There's also a lot fewer of those people here than in general. While we do have a few pot bellied grandpas, obese people are rare and almost everyone under 60 is a normal weight. Even the actual giants would still be on the smaller end of what would get posted here. They are also never found doing anything related to FA/HAES and also generally don't stay huge for very long. Hugely swollen fingers do make it hard to communicate after all.

However, we frequently have visitors from outside the community. Some of them will stay, but most of them don't. These visitors are just the general population, which means that most of them are severely obese. Plenty of them are just disrespectful jerks. However, when someone was reciting a story to me about such a visitor, it was very clear from the beginning that this person was way bigger than they should be. The term "waddle" was explicitly used (most people know and will occasionally use more specialized terminology like that), and there was no part of the story where anyone could EVER think that this person was of a normal weight. Apparently, the "subject" had such difficulty lifting their arms they couldn't even respond half the time.

We're generally hyper nice, but we don't have much mercy, especially not for huge outsiders.
